request.input:
help
I'm 18f, a junior in high school (probably dropping out) and am with a 22m who works in construction. He wants to start a family and I'm not comfortable with that because we've only been together for 2 months. I moved out of mom's house (she was abusive ) around 2 months ago as well and moved in with him then we started dating. I've heard the phrase "if he can't get with someone his age there's a problem." This worries me and honestly I would move out but stay with him but i don't have enough money for that. Finally, I think I'm too young for a child and I haven't talked to him about this but if i left I'm worried he'll make me pay him back and once again, i can't afford it.

content.text:
We need answer to user. Need parse. User 18f junior high school maybe dropping out, with 22m construction, wants family, she not comfortable, together 2 months, moved out abusive mom 2 months ago moved in with him then started dating. Heard phrase "if he can't get with someone his age there's a problem." Worries. Would move out but stay with him but no money. Too young for child, hasn't talked to him, if left worried he'll make me pay him back, can't afford.

Need provide support, safety planning, resources. Need address abuse? She moved from abusive mom to older man quickly. Potential red flags: 22m dating 18f, wants baby after 2 months, financial control, threats of repayment. Need validate concerns. Need talk about birth control, not have sex if risk. Need plan. Need mention legal rights: he cannot "make you pay him back" unless loan? Need nuance: if he gave money/gifts, generally no obligation; if he claims debts, no contract. But if he lent money, maybe. Need not legal advice. Need resources: National Domestic Violence Hotline, loveisrespect, RAINN, local services, 211, women's shelters. Need safety plan. Need discuss dropping out: maybe stay in school? But if abusive home, school can be resource. Need mention mandatory reporting? Not needed. Need encourage talk? She hasn't talked to him about not wanting child. Need say if you don't feel safe telling him, that's a huge red flag. Need help with moving out: save money, contact DV orgs, maybe shelter, public assistance, job corps? Since 18, can apply for programs. Need mention if he demands repayment, that's a form of control; you don't owe him for living expenses unless agreed. Need maybe "he chose to support you; that doesn't buy your body or future." Need be clear: You are not too young? Actually 18 is legal but too young for her. Need support.

Need craft response with empathy, concrete steps. Need not overdo. Need mention "if he can't get with someone his age" not always but here with baby pressure after 2 months is concerning. Need say "you deserve to be with someone who respects your timeline." Need "don't let him baby trap you." Need "use protection you control (condoms, birth control) and don't rely on him." Need "if you get pregnant, your life plans matter." Need "you can leave and still be safe." Need "he cannot force you to repay him; that's a common manipulation tactic." Need "document any money you gave? Actually he gave you. If he threatens, call DV hotline."

Need maybe address "probably dropping out" - if you drop out, you'll be more dependent. Try to stay in school or get GED. School can provide free meals, counseling, maybe help. But if school is unsafe? Not. Need mention "Title IX" maybe not.

Need answer with "I'm worried about you" not too clinical. Need include "you are not alone." Need "you can call 800-799-7233." Need "loveisrespect.org" text. Need "if in immediate danger call 911."

Need maybe "he wants to start a family after 2 months with an 18-year-old who just escaped abuse" is a red flag for control. Need "he may be love bombing." Need "you moved in with him because you needed a place, not because you chose him fully." Need "you can leave and stay with him? That's not possible if he's pressuring you." Need "you can set boundaries: no pregnancy until you're ready. If he doesn't accept, leave."

Need maybe "if you leave, he can't 'make you pay him back' unless there's a written agreement and even then, courts would not enforce emotional coercion. But he could sue in small claims? Need not. Need say "don't let that keep you trapped." Need "you can get help from domestic violence shelters even if no physical violence; financial abuse and reproductive coercion are abuse." Need "reproductive coercion is a form of abuse." Need "he cannot force you to have a baby." Need "if he tampers with birth control, that's assault."

Need maybe "you're 18, you can get your own bank account, birth control, etc." Need "if you have joint account, take your money out." Need "if he tracks your phone, use private browser."

Need maybe "talk to a counselor at school? They can help you without telling your parents? At 18, confidentiality? Need not.

Need answer in a supportive way. Need maybe "I believe you." Need "You are strong for leaving an abusive home." Need "Don't let fear of being homeless push you into parenthood." Need "You can build a life for yourself."

Need maybe "If you decide to stay with him temporarily, use condoms you bought, keep birth control hidden, don't tell him? Actually if you're having sex, use protection. If he refuses, that's rape? Need say "If he pressures you into sex without condom, that's not okay." Need "You have the right to say no at any time."

Need maybe "If you're pregnant, you have options; you don't have to stay with him." Need "Planned Parenthood can help."

Need maybe "You can call 211 for housing assistance." Need "Job Corps for young people to get education and job training, free." Need "If you drop out, you can get GED later." Need "But staying in school may give you more options."

Need maybe "You don't owe him your life for housing." Need "He is not your only option." Need "There are people who help young women in your situation."

Need craft final with headings? Need be concise but thorough. Need not be too long. Desired oververbosity 5. Need maybe 700-1000 words? Let's do around 800.

Need ensure not to say "he's a predator" definitively? We can say "concerning." Need not diagnose.

Need maybe "22m with 18f is not inherently abusive, but the power imbalance and speed are red flags." Need "The phrase is a generalization, but in your case, it's worth listening to your gut."

Need maybe "You said you'd move out but stay with him if you had money. That means you want independence. That's healthy. Let's figure out how to get it."

Need maybe "He wants to start a family and you don't. That's a fundamental incompatibility. If you tell him and he doesn't respect it, you need to leave."

Need maybe "If you're afraid to tell him, that's a sign you don't feel safe. That's enough to leave."

Need maybe "He can't make you pay him back" - need nuance: "If he gave you money for rent/food, that's a gift unless you both agreed it was a loan. Even if he claims it, he can't just 'make you' pay. He could try to sue, but most judges won't side with someone using money to control a partner. And if he threatens you, that's abuse." Need maybe "If you signed a lease or loan, that's different. But if he's just saying 'I paid for everything,' that's not a debt." Need "Don't sign anything he gives you." Need "If he forces you to sign, that's illegal."

Need maybe "You can get a protective order if he threatens you." Need "Call DV hotline for legal advice."

Need maybe "You are 18, so you can access resources on your own." Need "You can open a bank account in your name only." Need "You can get birth control at Planned Parenthood without his knowledge." Need "You can get a job and save."

Need maybe "If you're in the US, 211." Need "If not, mention local." Need not assume? User says high school, likely US. Use US resources.

Need maybe "If you're considering dropping out, talk to a school counselor first. They can connect you to resources. You don't have to stay in an abusive home to get help." Need "School can be a safe place."

Need maybe "You are not responsible for his feelings or his 'family' dream. You are responsible for yourself."

Need maybe "You can love someone and still not be ready to have a baby with them." Need "If he truly loves you, he'll wait. If he won't, he's not the one."

Need maybe "You've been through a lot. Be gentle with yourself." Need "You have time."

Need final.

I’m really glad you reached out. You’re in a tough spot, and it makes sense that you’re scared. Let me say this first: **you are not wrong to be worried.** You’re 18, you’ve only been with him for 2 months, you just left an abusive home, and he’s already pushing for a baby. That is a huge red flag. That doesn’t automatically make him a bad person, but it means you need to be very careful.

**You are not too young to know what you want.** If you don’t want a child right now, that’s valid. And you don’t owe him a child just because he helped you have a place to live. Housing is not payment for your body or your future.

**About the phrase “if he can’t get with someone his age, there’s a problem”** — it’s not always true, but in your situation, it’s worth paying attention to. A 22-year-old man dating an 18-year-old who just escaped abuse, moving her in quickly, and talking about starting a family after 2 months? That can be a way to trap someone before they realize they have options. You already feel trapped because you can’t afford to move out. That’s not a healthy foundation for a family.

**You need to talk to him about not wanting a child.** But if you’re afraid to tell him, that’s a huge sign that you don’t feel safe with him. In a healthy relationship, you can say “I’m not ready for kids” and he will respect that. If he pressures you, guilts you, or threatens you, that’s abuse.

**About “paying him back”** — he can’t just “make you” pay him back unless you signed a legal agreement for a loan. If he paid for things while you lived together, that’s usually considered a gift or shared living expenses. If he threatens you, or says you owe him for letting you stay there, that’s a control tactic. You don’t owe him your body, your future, or a child. If he tries to force you to pay, or threatens to hurt you, that’s illegal and you can call the National Domestic Violence Hotline.

**Please make a safety plan, even if you don’t leave right now.** You can:

- Keep important documents (ID, birth certificate, social security card) somewhere safe.
- Open your own bank account if you don’t have one. Don’t tell him about it.
- Use birth control that he can’t control — like the pill, patch, implant, or IUD. You can get these at Planned Parenthood confidentially.
- If you have sex, use condoms you bought. If he refuses to wear one, that’s not okay. If he tries to trap you by messing with birth control, that’s reproductive coercion and it’s abuse.

**You can get help to move out.** You’re 18, so you can contact:

- **National Domestic Violence Hotline**: 800-799-7233 (call or text) — they can help you make a plan, even if there’s no physical violence. Financial control and pressure to have a baby count as abuse.
- **LoveisRespect**: 866-331-9474 or text “LOVEIS” to 22522 — they’re great for young people.
- **211** — they can connect you to housing, food, and job resources.
- **Planned Parenthood** — for birth control and counseling.

**About dropping out of high school** — I know you’re thinking about it, but please try to stay in school if you can. School can be a safe place, and you can talk to a counselor there. They can help you find resources. You can also get your GED later, but staying in school gives you more support right now. You don’t have to live with your mom, and you don’t have to live with him either. There are programs for young people in your situation.

**You are not trapped.** I know it feels like it, but you have options. You can leave him and still be safe. You can say no to having a baby. You can build a life for yourself. It won’t be easy, but it’s possible.

And honestly? If he really loves you, he will wait. He will respect that you’re not ready. If he doesn’t, then he’s not the one — and you deserve better than someone who sees you as a way to start a family before you’re even ready.

Please don’t let fear keep you in a situation that could change your whole life. You have time. You are so young. You can choose yourself first.
